-3.15046,51.53050.name: CREATE Fertility Cardiff

-3.15046,51.53050.company: Satellite clinic to CREATE Fertility Bristol
-3.15046,51.53050.desc: A fertility clinic licensed and inspected by the Human Fertilisation and Embryology Authority. Satellite clinic to CREATE Fertility Bristol. A satellite is where patients are seen; the licence sits with the parent clinic, so the regulator's paperwork and the treatment are in different places. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. The HFEA licenses every clinic in the United Kingdom, inspects them, and publishes findings and success rates clinic by clinic. No other fertility regulator publishes at this level, which makes the UK the one country where this sector can be read rather than estimated.

Rats, mice and birds bred for research are excluded from the Act's definition of an animal — the overwhelming majority of animals used, and the great majority of the genetically altered ones. What is covered here is dogs, cats, primates, rabbits, guinea pigs, hamsters and farm animals. The rest is counted nowhere.

-72.97641,45.61853.name: Cégep de Saint-Hyacinthe
-72.97641,45.61853.status: Certificate of GAP Last visit: interim, December 2023
-72.97641,45.61853.desc: An institution certified by the Canadian Council on Animal Care for its use of animals in science. Certificate of GAP Last visit: interim, December 2023. CCAC certification is a condition of federal research funding rather than a licence, so an institution outside it is not necessarily outside the work — it may simply not take federal money. The CCAC publishes names and certificate status and no addresses, so this point marks the institution rather than the building where animals are held.

-87.62300,41.88500.name: International Society for Stem Cell Research — guidelines
-87.62300,41.88500.desc: Writes the guidelines the field actually follows on embryo models and on the fourteen-day limit, because in most countries no statute covers them. A professional body setting the rule where the law does not reach is the usual arrangement in this part of the sector, and it has no enforcement of any kind.

6.13000,49.58830.name: Eurofins Agroscience Services
6.13000,49.58830.desc: Assembled by buying up the agrochemical industry's established contract research laboratories and welding them into a single global offering, this arm of Eurofins conducts field and laboratory studies on new substances and new crop varieties and then also provides the regulatory service that compiles the resulting dossier. It states plainly that it supports plant breeders and the seed industry as well as pesticide manufacturers. Consolidation matters here more than size: when the independent laboratories that once checked each other are bought into one company, a second opinion becomes a second department.

-82.99880,39.96120.name: Battelle
-82.99880,39.96120.desc: A large non-profit research institute with a crop protection practice covering regulatory affairs, dossier preparation and field-based measurement of how sprayed material moves and settles. Its staff biographies describe carrying techniques developed for defence work into agricultural clients. It belongs here because it is the least commercial-looking organisation in this facet and does the same work: a non-profit institute preparing regulatory submissions for industry is still preparing them for the applicant, and the reader should not read the tax status as independence.
